text: The key to everything: engineering soon How to formulate clear instructions to create educational resources adapted to your classroom. title: Comparison of Prompts
text: Comparison of Prompts SIMPLE PROMPT "Make a text about the water cycle." Generic and unadapted result. ADVANCED PROMPT [ROL] He acts as a teacher of Natural Sciences of Primary. [ACTION] It creates an explanatory text about the water cycle. [CONTEXT] The text is for students of 4th Primary (9-10 years) with a basic reading level. [FORMAT] Structure it in three short paragraphs: 1. Evaporation, 2. Condensation and Precipitation, 3. Collection. Use a clear, simple language with easy to understand analogies. title: Work Frameworks for Prompts Experts
text: Work Frameworks for Prompts Experts RITA, CARE and RTF: three aid to order the petition RITA An ideal framework to quickly structure a petition, ensuring that AI understands who it should be, what to do, how to communicate it and who. Role: It defines the personality that AI should adopt (expert, tutor, etc.) to contextualize the answer. Instruction: The specific and clear task that must be performed. It is the main action of the prompt. To: Determines the style of communication (formal, creative, informal) to adjust to the target. Audience: It specifies who directs the result to adapt vocabulary and complexity. Example: "Acts like a museum guide (Roll) . It explains the importance of Picasso's 'Guernica' (Instruction) with one passionate and informative tone (To) for the first time High School Students ( Audiencia) ." Example with sources · secondary and FP

title: Role · Instruction · To · Audience
text: Role · Instruction · To · Audience "Acts as a museum guide. Explains the context of Guernica with an informative tone for baccalaureate. Use the attached sources and identify the claims to be contrasted." CARE Excellent for tasks requiring precision and a specific result, guiding AI with a clear model. Context: It provides the necessary background information for AI to understand the "why" of the task. Action: The main verb that defines the task to be executed (create, summarize, compare, etc.). Result: It describes the desired final product, including structure, key elements and format. Example: It offers a specific model that AI can imitate to ensure maximum precision. Example: " We are studying the Industrial Revolution (Context) . Create (Action) a comparative table with 3 columns (advantages, disadvantages, key inventions) (Resulted) . For example, an advantage could be 'Mass production' (Example) ." Example with sources · secondary and FP

title: Context · Action · Result · Example
text: Context · Action · Result · Example "We study the Industrial Revolution. Compare two changes in a table with impact and source. As a row model, it uses: change → consequence → evidence of the dossier." RTF A direct and efficient model, perfect for when the task and output format are the main priority. Role: It defines the expert profile that must assume AI to orient the content. Task: The objective or work to do, described in a concise and direct way. Format: The desired output structure (list, table, paragraph, JSON, etc.), crucial to structured responses. Example: "You are one nutrition expert (Rool) . Prepare a healthy weekly menu (Tasca) ⁇ ⁇ nested list format, separating by days and meals (dinner, dinner) (formed) ." Example with sources · secondary and FP

title: An answer can mix correct and invented data
text: An answer can mix correct and invented data Reference Document: "La biblioteca obre dilluns i dimecres de 9 a 11 h. El préstec dura 14 dies." Simulated response: "You can go to the library Monday and Wednesday from 9 am to 11 am, and also Friday afternoon. The loan lasts 14 days and can be renewed automatically." What statements can you justify with the document? See analysis With support: days and times indicated, and duration of 14 days. Without support: Opening Friday and automatic renewal. The document does not confirm them; we can not give them for certain. Revised version: "According to the document, the library opens Mondays and Wednesdays from 9 am to 11 pm and the loan lasts 14 days. There is no information about other schedules or renovations." Asking the same AI to be reviewed is not an independent contrast It can help find problems, but it is necessary to check the evidence. If you cannot verify a relevant statement, identify it as uncertain or exclude it from the material. Proposal for the work of iAducació. 04 INSTRUCTIONS WE CAN REUS

text: A reusable configuration to start Objective: To help the teacher create comprehension questions for [level]. Sources: works with the dossier facilitated. Indicates the fragment or support page. text: Educational Assistants and Agentive AI A GPT, Gem or reusable procedure is not automatically an AI agent. title: What support do you support the guidance of 2026?
text: What support do you support the guidance of 2026? Institutional orientation, not a new law. The teacher defines the criteria and evaluates first. You can then use AI as a support to review or contrast, without delegating the professional trial. The OIA-36 and 37 must be read together. [35 · p. 38] [35 · p. 39] Planned Support Limit to maintain Prepare instruments and descriptors of levels Criteria previously defined by the teacher. Correct unequivocal responses or limited multiple options Check solutions and data processing; not extrapolate to open assessments of the student. Identify error patterns and suggest comments With previous teaching criteria and within the limits of the OIA-37; not to determine achievements or individual progress. Improve the expression of the return Part of comments made by the teacher, preserving the sense. The document indicates that AI should not be used to define evaluation criteria, check whether the evidence covers all criteria or automatically generates feedback. Nor does it present evaluation or qualification with AI as an ordinary use solved with a final validation: high-risk uses require legal and documentary requirements. [35 · p. 38] [35 · p. 39]

title: Works, authorship and human revision
text: Works, authorship and human revision Do not share works that identify students, contain personal experiences or are creative productions (reactions, drawings, photographs or music). Pseudonimization remains personal data processing. [35 · p. 39] [35 · p. 40]

text: A process that leaves a trace Define learning Provides reliable sources Generate a draft Check content and accessibility Try a short task Publish the revised version Template: A Revisitable Learning Situation Educational proposal of iAducació · uses own or authorized materials and fictitious data. It develops activities for a [duration] learning situation about [rest], for [level], from these decisions that I have already defined as a teacher: [objects, knowledge, exact reference criteria, formative evaluation moments and support measures]. Add a list of checks for the teacher. Example: ESO and FP with the same challenge Fictional challenge: reduce waste from a workshop. In ESO, analyze fictitious data and argue a proposal. title: Ages, authorizations and guarantees of the center
text: Ages, authorizations and guarantees of the center Department orientations (2026). It is necessary to distinguish the legal basis of the treatment, the conditions of each service and the educational decisions of the center. [35 · p. 12] Under 14: Avoid the autonomous use of general-purpose AI. Literacy with the teacher operating the tool and the students observing and reflecting. Specific educational tools require checking the institutional requirements. [35 · p. 25] From 14 to 18 years old: The document explains that ordinary educational use is based, in general, on the mission of public interest; it recommends family authorization as an additional guarantee and warns that the service contract may require it. Informing families remains necessary. [35 · p. 12] Organizational guidelines: The document places direct interaction from the second quarter of 3rd ESO, with the corresponding authorization and the exception indicated for the inflexibility of basic education. It does not replace checking the actual age, tool conditions and circumstances of each student. In FP it is also necessary to distinguish minor and older students. [35 · p. 13] The center manages the authorizations when they perceive and configure accesses to reflect the agreed uses. Annex 5 is a Adaptable Model , not a universal authorization for all platforms. [35 · p. 20] Model of authorization, p. 67–69 .

title: From natural language to a prototype we can try
text: From natural language to a prototype we can try LA PETITION "Create a cost simulator: €5 fixed and €3 per piece. Explain how the total change." ● ● ● Cost of a production 5 pieces → 20 € Genera A small, understandable prototype. Test Extreme values, keyboard and results. Corrects Check before using it in the classroom. A fictional example of iAducació. The relation is cost = 5 + 3 × pieces; they are not data from a company. In this course we use vibe coding to discuss the iterative creation of code with AI help: to describe, generate, test and correct. It is a working definition; it does not mean that the code is safe or correct without review.

title: Minimum tests before publishing
text: Minimum tests before publishing Test Check Content Formulas, units, answers and limits with examples calculated by hand. Accessibility Keyboard, visible focus, labels, contrast and alternative text. Data and security No real names, secret keys, hidden tracking or charges to unforeseen services. Operation Mobile, small screen, input errors and limited connection. Maintenance Save the code, a version and the revision instructions. Template: generates an autonomous HTML activity Educational proposal of iAducació · uses own or authorized materials and fictitious data. Create an activity in an autonomous HTML on [concept]. It must include short instructions, tag controls, keyboard use and explanations of the answers. Do not use external services, analytics, accounts or personal data. Set editable content. It includes three test cases and the limitations of the model. All results must be reviewed by the teacher. The value is pedagogical AI facilitates prototyping; deciding if the activity helps to understand it remains a teaching job. UNESCO recommends validating the educational adaptation of the tools. [8]

title: Extending tasks, preserving learning
text: Extending tasks, preserving learning The OIA-34 proposes websites and escape games as examples of more complex products that AI can help build. The conception, orientation and criterion remain of the students. [35 · p. 36] It preserves technical and accessibility tests. It declares the help received and asks for an explanation of the operation. If AI executes autonomous actions on services, accounts or files, it is no longer just to generate code: the AI-10 discourages the adoption of agent AI in educational environments. title: How do you train?
text: How do you train? Training a machine learning model is to adjust the parameters to improve the result with respect to a goal. The data, the objective and the evaluation process condition what you learn and where you can fail. [3] [6] DELIVERY IS NOT ONLY Amounted Data

title: 1. Prepare
text: 1. Prepare Select, review and separate data according to its function.

title: 2. Adjust
text: 2. Adjust Compare results with the target and modify parameters.

title: 3. Evaluate
text: 3. Evaluate Check behavior with examples not used to train. Validation helps to adjust the design; the final test evaluates reserved data. Original vector diagram of iAducació · didactic synthesis based on [3] [6] . It does not represent measures or a complete architecture.

title: Training
text: Training Examples that fit the parameters of the model.

title: Validation
text: Validation Data to compare configurations and guide development decisions.

title: Test
text: Test Data reserved for the final evaluation of the selected model. There is no universal percentage for each set. It is necessary to avoid duplicates and filtering between sets. [6]

title: In the case of LLM
text: In the case of LLM Pre-training: Learning linguistic patterns through tasks such as predicting tokens. [5] Later adjustment: Additional training to follow instructions or adapt to a task. Specific techniques vary between models. [5] [7] Evaluation: check results with different examples from those used to adjust the model. [6] A conversation does not mean to retrain the model Give instructions or examples in a prompt orients the answer through context, without modifying the parameters itself. The possible subsequent use of conversations by the supplier is a different question, regulated by their conditions. title: AI specialized
text: AI specialized A concrete task It detects patterns to do a specific job. Examples: Identify spam. Convert a voice-to-text recording with a transcription system. title: General purpose AI
text: General purpose AI Many tasks with the same model A general-purpose model can make a wide range of tasks and integrate into different applications. For example, it can summarize, create activities or help program. Examples with the same model: To summarize a text and highlight the main ideas. Propose questions to work on reading comprehension. Reform an explanation with a simpler vocabulary. Suggest activities on a topic for different levels. Help to understand and correct a code fragment. Your answers must be reviewed. title: General AI (AGI)
text: General AI (AGI) A capacity still in research The objective is to learn and apply knowledge in very diverse areas, with a capacity comparable to human. Concept of research; it is not a capacity that can be given to achieve by doing several tasks. [19] Doing many tasks is not the same as having a general intelligence. title: Other ways to classify AI
text: Other ways to classify AI The following categories answer different questions and can be combined. The same system can be generative, multimodal and based on deep learning. title: Rules or learning
text: Rules or learning Based on knowledge: It operates with explicit representations and rules. Machine learning: It obtains patterns from the data. The approaches can be combined. [1] [3] According to the purpose

title: Predict or generate
text: Predict or generate Predictive or discriminative: loves values or distinguishes categories. Generative: produces new content such as text, images or audio. [3] According to data

title: A modality or several
text: A modality or several Unimodal: It works with a type, as text. Multimodal: It combines modalities, such as text and images; inputs and outputs are dependent on the model. [13] According to access

title: Service or weights available
text: Service or weights available We can use a hosted service or deploy models with available weights, depending on license and resources. Having available weights does not imply that everything is free or that all licenses are equivalent. [13] BETWEEN CONCEPTS Artificial intelligence Machine learning Deep Learning

text: Areas included within other areas Deep learning is a part of machine learning, which in turn is part of AI. Current LLMs are based on deep neural networks. text: 3. Protect data before sharing them You must avoid entering personal data of own or third parties . In the analysis of data center, aggregate information and prevention of identification of people is prioritized. Family authorizations must be handled according to the context and conditions of the service: they do not replace the other guarantees. Personal data, p. 13 · Authorizations and data analysis, pp. 20–22 .

title: 4. Evaluate the process and maintain the teaching trial
text: 4. Evaluate the process and maintain the teaching trial It is recommended to collect drafts, oral explanations, reviews and evidence of the process . The teacher makes the assessment first; the subsequent support of AI must be limited. The document discourages the evaluations. AI detectors , because of the errors and risks they carry, and stresses learning. Evaluation, pp. 37–40 .

text: 5. A centre, shared and revisable agreement The incorporation of AI requires common criteria, training of the cloister and information to families The framework of responsible use must specify tools, responsibilities and monitoring mechanisms; it is not only an individual choice of each teacher.
